The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men’s basketball team** was the breakthrough group that turned Harvard into a modern national story: they won the **Ivy League**, made the **NCAA tournament**, and earned **Harvard’s first-ever NCAA tournament win**.

## Snapshot
- **Season:** 2011–12
- **Conference:** Ivy League
- **Head coach:** **Tommy Amaker**
- **Overall record:** **26–5**
- **Ivy League record:** **12–2**
- **Postseason:** **NCAA Tournament (West Region)**
  - **Round of 64:** Harvard (12) def. Vanderbilt (5), **59–54**
  - **Round of 32:** Wisconsin (4) def. Harvard (12), **51–49**

## Why this team mattered
### 1) Ivy champions and a program win record
Harvard finished **26–5**, which was a **program record for wins** at the time, and won the **Ivy League title** (earning the league’s automatic NCAA bid).

### 2) A landmark NCAA Tournament win
Harvard’s win over **Vanderbilt** in the 2012 NCAA Tournament was:
- **Harvard’s first NCAA Tournament game win** (the program had appeared before, but hadn’t won a game)
- The **first Ivy League NCAA Tournament win since 1998** (Princeton over UCLA)

They then nearly reached the Sweet 16, losing to **Wisconsin by 2 points**.

### 3) The midseason academic scandal
A defining part of the season was the highly publicized February 2012 academic integrity case:
- **Kyle Casey** and **Brandyn Curry** (key players/captains) **withdrew from the team** late in the season amid allegations tied to academic misconduct.
- Despite losing important rotation pieces just before postseason play, Harvard **still finished the job**, won the Ivy title, and made the NCAA run—one reason this team is remembered as unusually resilient.

## Key personnel (high-level)
### Coach
- **Tommy Amaker** — by 2011–12 he had established an NBA/major-conference style program culture and recruiting footprint at Harvard, and this season became his national coming-out moment at the school.

### Star player
- **Keith Wright (F/C)** — the team’s interior anchor and top all-around scorer/rebounder.
  - **Ivy League Player of the Year (2011–12)** (widely recognized as the league’s best player that season)

### Other notable contributors (non-exhaustive)
Harvard’s identity was balanced: half-court execution, spacing/shooting, strong team defense, and veteran leadership. Among the prominent rotation players were:
- **Oliver McNally (G)** — senior guard/leader and major perimeter piece
- **Laurent Rivard (G)** — elite three-point shooting threat who helped define Harvard’s spacing
- **Christian Webster (G)** — key guard who took on bigger responsibility, especially after the late-season roster losses
- **Wesley Saunders (W/F)** — impactful freshman wing who became an important two-way contributor
- **Kyle Casey (F)** and **Brandyn Curry (G)** — significant players early in the year before withdrawing in February

## Style of play (what they were known for)
- **Disciplined half-court offense**: patient possessions, strong shot selection, lots of emphasis on spacing and execution.
- **Perimeter shooting + post presence**: Wright inside plus multiple credible outside shooters created matchup problems.
- **Composure in close games**: reflected both experience (upperclassmen) and Amaker’s control-oriented approach.

## Legacy
This season is commonly cited as the moment Harvard men’s basketball fully entered the national conversation:
- It validated Amaker’s long-term rebuild
- It created an identity for Harvard basketball beyond the Jeremy Lin era (Lin had left two seasons earlier)
- It helped recruiting and raised expectations—Harvard became a regular contender for Ivy titles in the following years

If you want, I can also compile (1) the full roster with class/position, (2) game-by-game results, or (3) the NCAA Tournament game recaps and key late-game sequences vs Vanderbilt and Wisconsin.
